label: Second copy step (input orig[1], outputting orig[2]) in length-5/6 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at the step two after <DEL>: the input is the echoed second original token and the model is outputting the third original token (recall_idx == 2, so prev2_tok is <DEL>). It fires on about 32% of recall_idx==2 steps over all lengths, but its firing depends heavily on sequence length: L=5 fires on nearly every such step (precision ~0.99) and carries 67% of the mass, L=6 carries 30%, L=4 fires weakly and only sometimes (~2% of mass), and L>=7 or L=3 almost never fires. Within this slot, token identity matters little. The highest activations come when the first token is t or y. It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, or at any other recall position (recall_idx 1 or 3 together hold under 0.5% of mass). Missed activations are mostly weak L=4 cases.

issues: I reproduced the test scores exactly for (recall_idx==2)&isin(L,[5,6]): P 0.882, R 0.894, F1 0.888, mass recall 0.968.

The profile supports the factual claims. On the original and delimiter phases the feature has 0 activations. In the copy phase, recall_idx==2 holds 99.6% of the mass, recall_idx 1 holds 0.1% and recall_idx 3 holds 0.3%. By length, L=5 holds 67.1%, L=6 30.1%, L=4 2.2% and L=7 0.6%. L=3, 8 and 9 hold about 0.

The predicate splits unevenly by length. Precision is 0.987 at L=5 but only 0.778 at L=6 (dev and test similar). So about 22% of L=6 slot steps stay inactive, and these make up nearly all of the roughly 19k test false positives.
The explanation does not separate the L=5 and L=6 precisions; it only gives about 0.99 for L=5.

Inside the L=6 slot, how often the feature fires depends weakly and diffusely on the tokens. By first_tok, precision runs from 0.81 to 0.97. Sequences with repeated tokens score 0.71 and sequences with 2 or more digits score 0.83. There is no clean token class to carve out, so I treat this as graded modulation, not a systematic counterexample.

Misses on the test split are mostly weak L=4 activations at step 6 (relative magnitude about 0.03 to 0.24), plus rare L=7 cases. Together they hold 3.2% of the mass, which matches the explanation. Adding L=4 to the predicate would hurt precision, because only about 14% of L=4 slot steps fire.
The claim that the top activations start with t or y holds: prev_tok, which is orig(0) at this step, shows the highest lift for y and t.
